title: BioXend pipeline parameters
description: MIX-MB ChEMBL submission file generator — converts a filled MIX-MB template into six ChEMBL-ready deposition files.

input_output_options.title: Input / output
input_output_options.description: Where to find the input template and where to write the output files.

input.description: Path to your filled MIX-MB submission template (.ods).
input.help_text: Download the blank template from `Standards/Templates/Template_open.ods` from the GitHub repository https://github.com/zmahnoor14/BioXend/blob/devel/Standards/Templates/Template_open.ods, fill in all five sheets (Reference, Chemicals, Microbes, Experiment, Biotransformation), upload it on your s3 bucket on CloWM. The file must have the `.ods` extension. To test out the workflow, use the `Try it out` button.

outdir.description: Directory where the seven ChEMBL deposition files will be written. Choose your output directory from your data bucket on CloWM.
outdir.help_text: The pipeline writes `REFERENCE.tsv`, `README.toml`, `COMPOUND_RECORD.tsv`, `COMPOUND_CTAB.sdf`, `ASSAY.tsv`, `ASSAY_PARAM.tsv`, and `ACTIVITY.tsv` into this directory. The directory is created automatically if it does not exist.

compound_options.title: Compound options
compound_options.description: Options that control how compound identifiers are generated.

prefix.description: Short alphanumeric prefix for auto-generated compound IDs (CIDXs).
prefix.help_text: Compounds are numbered sequentially from this prefix, e.g. `CIDX` produces `CIDX0001`, `CIDX0002`, etc. Choose a prefix that reflects your study: typically derived from your Reference Identifier filled in the Reference sheet e.g: HumanMicrobiomeDrugMetabolism reference identifier has compound identifier prefixes as HMDM. Must start with a letter and contain only letters (2–30 characters). Sequential numbering is generated by the workflow.

xenobiotic_class.description: Singular class name for the compounds in this study, used in ASSAY_DESCRIPTION, e.g: `drug`, `pesticide`, `xenobiotic compound`.
xenobiotic_class.help_text: This term appears in the generated assay description text, e.g. 'Biotransformation of [xenobiotic_class] by ...'. Use a singular noun that best describes your compound class. Common values: `drug`, `pesticide`, `food additive`, `environmental contaminant`, `xenobiotic compound`.

pipeline_options.title: Pipeline options
pipeline_options.description: General options that control pipeline behaviour.

strict.description: Fail the pipeline on any validation warning.
strict.help_text: By default the pipeline logs validation warnings and continues. Set `--strict` to treat any warning as a fatal error — recommended before final ChEMBL submission to ensure clean output files.
